questions.question: A vertical rectangular gate 3.0 m high and 2.0 m wide is flush with the water surface. The hydrostatic force on it is closest to:
questions.explanation: For a surface starting at the free surface, F = ρ g b h^2 / 2 = 1000·9.8·2·3^2/2 ≈ 8.8×10^4 N = 88 kN.
steps: Use F = ρ g b h^2 / 2
questions.fastStrategy: Surface to depth h: force ≈ 0.5·ρg·b·h^2.

questions.question: For the same 3.0 m gate, the center of pressure below the surface is at:
questions.explanation: For a vertical plane from the surface, y_cp = 2h/3 = 2 m below the free surface.
questions.fastStrategy: Flat plate from surface: center of pressure at 2/3 depth.

questions.question: A U-tube manometer with water shows a 18 cm difference between legs. Gauge pressure in the connected line is about:
questions.fastStrategy: Roughly 10 kPa per meter of water; 0.18 m → ~1.8 kPa.

questions.question: A 5.0 cm³ air bubble at 30 m depth (fresh water) rises to the surface at constant temperature. Its surface volume is closest to:
questions.explanation: Absolute pressure at 30 m ≈ 101 kPa + ρgh ≈ 101 + 294 ≈ 395 kPa (~3.9 atm). P1V1 = P2V2 → V2 ≈ 3.9×5 ≈ 20 cm³.
questions.fastStrategy: Each 10 m water ≈ 1 atm; ~4 atm at 30 m → ~4× volume at surface.

questions.question: A circular viewport of radius 0.50 m is 10 m below sea water (ρ≈1030). Hydrostatic force on the window is closest to:
questions.fastStrategy: P ≈ 0.1 MPa at 10 m; multiply by ~0.8 m² → ~8×10^4 N.

questions.question: A Venturi meter has 0.30 m inlet and 0.15 m throat. If ΔP = 8 kPa for water, the flow rate is closest to:
questions.fastStrategy: Throat area ~0.018; ΔP 8 kPa water → throat speed ~4 m/s → Q ≈ 0.07.

questions.question: For water (ρ=1000, μ=1.0×10^-3 Pa·s) flowing at 2.0 m/s in a 5 cm pipe, the Reynolds number is closest to:
questions.fastStrategy: Rule: water Re ≈ 1e6·D(m)·v; here 1e6·0.05·2 ≈ 1e5.

questions.question: Darcy-Weisbach head loss: water, f = 0.02, length 50 m, diameter 0.10 m, velocity 3.0 m/s. Head loss is closest to:
Pump power to lift 0.50 m³/s of water by 15 m (neglect losses) is closest to:
questions.fastStrategy: Rule: 10 kN/m³ × 0.5 × 15 ≈ 75 kW.

questions.question: Water bulk modulus ≈ 2.2 GPa. A 5 MPa pressure rise causes a volume decrease of about:
Air in a syringe is 30 mL at 1 atm. Compressed isothermally to 10 mL, the absolute pressure is about:
questions.fastStrategy: Volume shrinks to 1/3 → pressure triples (isothermal ideal gas).

questions.question: A point is 4 m below water overlain by 3 m of oil (ρ=800). Gauge pressure at the point is closest to:
questions.explanation: Oil column: 800·9.8·3 ≈ 23.5 kPa; water column: 1000·9.8·4 ≈ 39.2 kPa. Sum ≈ 62.7 kPa.
questions.fastStrategy: Add 8 kPa per m of oil + 9.8 kPa per m of water → ~24 + 39 = 63 kPa.

questions.question: Water discharges from a 0.010 m² orifice under 2.0 m head with Cd = 0.62. Flow rate is closest to:
questions.fastStrategy: Orifice: Q ≈ 0.62 A sqrt(2gh); here ~0.04 m³/s.

questions.question: Air (ρ≈1.2) at 60 kPa static flows 30 m/s. Stagnation pressure is closest to:
questions.explanation: Dynamic pressure q = 0.5 ρ v^2 = 0.5·1.2·900 ≈ 540 Pa = 0.54 kPa. Total ≈ 60 + 0.54 ≈ 60.5 kPa.
questions.fastStrategy: q ≈ 0.6 kPa at 30 m/s air; add to static.

questions.question: Specific weight γ of mercury (ρ≈13,600 kg/m³) is closest to:
questions.fastStrategy: Water is ~9.8 kN/m³; mercury ~13.6× → ~133 kN/m³.

questions.question: A Pitot tube in water shows a 1.2 m head difference. Flow speed is closest to:
questions.explanation: Pitot gives v ≈ sqrt(2 g h) = sqrt(2·9.8·1.2) ≈ sqrt(23.5) ≈ 4.85 m/s.
questions.fastStrategy: Each meter of water head gives ~4.4 m/s; 1.2 m → ~4.9 m/s.

questions.question: A differential manometer uses fluid SG 1.5. A 0.25 m height difference indicates a pressure difference of about:
questions.fastStrategy: Use excess density (500 kg/m³) × g × 0.25 m → ~1.2 kPa.

questions.question: A pump delivers 18 kg/s of water. The volumetric flow rate is:
questions.fastStrategy: Water: move decimal three left when converting kg/s to m³/s.

questions.question: Water pressure of 200 kPa corresponds to a head of approximately:
questions.fastStrategy: Use 10 kPa ≈ 1.02 m of water; 200 kPa ≈ 20 m.

questions.question: For water in a 2.0 cm diameter tube, what speed gives Re ≈ 2000? (ρ=1000, μ=1.0×10^-3)
A 1.0 mm diameter sphere (ρ=2500) falls in water (ρ=1000, μ=1.0×10^-3) at low Re. Stokes terminal speed is closest to:
questions.fastStrategy: Plug into Stokes; tiny sphere squared drops speed heavily.

questions.question: A fluid has density 880 kg/m³. Its specific gravity (water=1) is:
questions.fastStrategy: Move decimal three left vs water density.

questions.question: A tank shows a vacuum (negative gauge) of -20 kPa. Atmospheric pressure is 101 kPa. Absolute pressure in the tank is:
questions.fastStrategy: Vacuum reading subtracts from atmospheric to get absolute.

questions.question: In a hydraulic lift, a 3 cm² input piston supports a 120 cm² output piston. Applying 400 N on the small piston ideally lifts:
questions.explanation: Force multiplies by area ratio. 120/3 = 40. Output ≈ 400·40 = 16,000 N.
questions.fastStrategy: Area ratio 40× → force 40× (ideal).

questions.question: A water jet of 0.80 kg/s strikes a flat plate and stops. Jet speed is 25 m/s. Ideal force on the plate is:
questions.explanation: Momentum flux F = ṁ v = 0.80·25 = 20 N (assuming full stop, normal impact).
questions.fastStrategy: Force equals mass flow times velocity change; here 0.8×25.
